title: How a Bicycle Works
intro: A bicycle turns your leg power into forward motion through a chain that spins the back wheel.
summary: Pedals turn the crank, the chain carries that spin to the rear sprocket, and the rear wheel rolls the bike forward while the frame holds everything together.
photo: A real photo shows a metal or carbon frame shaped like a diamond, two wheels with thin spoked rims and rubber tires, a chain running over a front chain ring and a small rear cog, pedals on crank arms, a handlebar on top of the front fork, and a padded saddle on a seat post.

parts.label: Main frame
parts.say: The frame is the backbone that holds the wheels, seat, and handlebar together. Its tubes form a strong triangle.

parts.label: Rear wheel
parts.say: The rear wheel is the part that pushes the bike forward. The chain spins it.

parts.label: Front wheel
parts.say: The front wheel steers the bike. It turns freely and is not driven by the chain.

parts.label: Chain and pedals
parts.say: Pedals turn the chain ring, and the chain pulls the rear cog. That spin is what moves the bike.

parts.label: Handlebar
parts.say: The handlebar lets you steer. It turns the front fork and wheel.

parts.label: Saddle
parts.say: The saddle is where the rider sits. It sits on top of the seat post.
